artworks.title: Hypsipyle Saves Thoas
artworks.description: BnF illumination (Français 599): Hypsipyle smuggles her father Thoas from the Lemnian massacre — medieval Boccaccio reception of the Argonaut island's spared king.

artworks.title: Hypsipyle Sparing Her Father Thoas
artworks.description: Woodcut: Hypsipyle saves Thoas while Opheltes dies in the background — the Lemnian king as father spared and later myth's crossroads.

popCulture.title: Argonautica
popCulture.creator: Apollonius of Rhodes
popCulture.description: Book I — Thoas' Lemnos after the women kill the men; Hypsipyle rules in her father's stead when the Argo lands.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus' Lemnian crime — Thoas hidden in a chest and cast to sea, the father Hypsipyle alone would not kill.

popCulture.title: Thoas (king of Lemnos)
popCulture.description: Dionysus' son, Hypsipyle's father — spared when the Lemnian women kill every other man on the island.
